page: Amazon Web Services m7i.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 128 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, which provides a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network-based resources.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7i.8xlarge demonstrates strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.91 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 46.4 GB/sec. Geekbench scores are also strong, with a single-core score of 2048.0 and a multi-core score of 16303.0. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. These instructions contribute to a top-tier text generation speed of 413.98 tokens per second during LLM inference with a small 135M model, though performance scales down to 2.79 tokens per second for a large 70B model.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the m7i.8xlarge is characterized by its modern DDR5 memory and dedicated Gen7 Intel Xeon architecture, which deliver high resource density for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space must rely on network storage, which is capped at a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. This instance is best suited for enterprise applications, web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
